A1.justification: Despite the changed title and layout, both PDFs describe the same DisCo study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DisCo experiments on DiverseHumans and MultiHuman-TestBench, including benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, supplementary analyses, and qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same Flow-GRPO procedure, four reward components, facial embedding pipeline, and single-stage curriculum. No algorithmic component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both use 30,000 training prompts involving 2–7 people, the 1,200-prompt DiverseHumans evaluation with four diversity-tag conditions, and MultiHuman-TestBench. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within both benchmark blocks of Table 1 and the appendix comparisons. For example, SD3.5 remains included only in Table 1's DiverseHumans block; the other baseline rows and appendix subsets are retained.

E3.justification: The stated training budgets, sampling settings, resolutions, evaluation sample information, and baseline configurations are unchanged. Appendices C–D retain the same metrics, detection and similarity thresholds, and clustering procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablation, reward-weight search, aggregation-function comparison, diversity-tag and person-count analyses, training curves, and qualitative reward-hacking examples. These analyses are relocated or reformatted without changing their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: The person-count plot retains its stated 95% confidence intervals, moving from Figure 4 to Figure 5. Appendix D retains image-index seeds shared across evaluations; no repeated-run or statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries match in Tables 1–2 and E.1–E.4. For example, DisCo(Flux) retains 92.4% Count Accuracy, 98.6% UFA, and 98.3% GIS on DiverseHumans. The plots and qualitative examples retain the same findings.

T1.justification: The flow/MDP/SDE formulation, GRPO objective, reward definitions, curriculum mathematics, and evaluation metric definitions are unchanged. Equation renumbering, regrouping, and shortened distribution notation are presentation edits.

C1.justification: Both claim annotation-free improvements in intra-image and cross-sample identity diversity, counting, and visual quality. v2 foregrounds cross-sample diversity and replaces the abstract's 'first RL-based' wording with 'novel,' but retains the no-prior-approach assertion in the introduction and the same substantive contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of group diversity, count/HPS regularization, and curriculum benefits are retained. Appendix F preserves the same occlusion, pose, and small-face limitations and future directions. The revised summaries emphasize interpretations already developed in v1.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, pseudocode, and code/data access information are retained. The Reproducibility statement moves from the main text to the appendix's end without losing its information.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage and substantive contrast with prior generation and RL methods remain unchanged. Updates to the Black, Lee, and Stable Diffusion references revise bibliographic metadata for corresponding works rather than introduce new literature.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and revises the abstract, introductory passages, and conclusion to emphasize cross-sample diversity. Ethics and Reproducibility move to the appendix's end, and citation formatting changes. Most methodological, experimental, and supplementary prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 1–2 and 4–5 exchange order, table captions change placement, and appendix pages are reformatted. The displays retain the existing scientific evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing cross-sample diversity contribution more explicit in its opening and conclusion, while adding specific arXiv identifiers to the retained Black and Lee references improves traceability. These are modest communication gains; the empirical evidence, technical documentation, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
